title: How Alex Slater scaled Quitter: Stripe paywall to skip Apple's fee and 20% daily ad spend increases
summary: A Miami vlog week where Alex Slater, founder of the Quitter app, shares two concrete growth levers: a Stripe web paywall that avoids Apple's cut, and raising ad spend 20% a day while profitable. He also covers bringing in an experienced investor, cutting operational waste, and choosing a high-energy location.

principles.text: Route eligible users to a Stripe paywall to skip Apple's ~30% fee and lift proceeds without growing gross revenue.
principles.quote: It was more like 30%. But that's the fees that we would pay to Apple that we're now negating and uh just taking the cut through Stripe.

principles.text: Roll out a new monetization path as a small test (10% of users) and expand only once data shows it's more profitable.
principles.quote: Right now it's just a 10% test. So 10% of users see the strike pay wall. you know, as we get the data back and as we see it's like way more profitable, we're going to uh introduce it to everyone.

principles.text: Scale ad spend by 20% a day as long as it stays profitable, tracking gross versus proceeds after platform cuts.
principles.quote: boosting ad spend by 20% a day on the note that it's profitable. Like if it remains profitable, this number should jump by 20% every single day.

principles.text: Bring in an experienced investor or advisor when they can tell you what to focus on and save months of guessing.
principles.quote: it's easier for someone with more experience to come in and like tell you what to focus your time on rather than you guessing and trying to figure it out yourself.

principles.text: Audit operations regularly and cut waste fast; shutting down bloat as soon as it appears is a relief and unlocks growth.
principles.quote: it feels very relieving to finally cut it out and to see it and to like shut it down as soon as it pops up.

principles.text: Optimize for speed over comfort: choose the environment that keeps you moving fast rather than slowing your plans down.
principles.quote: Rather like move fast. Why be the horse when you can be the Ferrari?
